sections.heading: 00 — README
sections.intro:
**Polymer Ph.D. — Drone Flight knowledge package**

This folder contains a synthesised knowledge base built from **3 YouTube transcripts** from the
channel **[DansTube.TV](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCa10m04VDy8yJghT3eJET9Q)**, all covering
setup, settings, and flight technique for the DJI Air 3S.

---

sections.heading: What this is
sections.intro:
**This package synthesises three videos from one YouTube channel about one drone.** That is its
scope and its whole content today. Every claim in it traces back to a specific video, at a
specific timestamp.

**Nothing in this package originates outside the transcripts.**

---

sections.heading: What was processed
sections.intro:
| Measure | Figure |
|---|---|
| Videos written up as structured notes | **3** |
| Source channel | **DansTube.TV** |
| Knowledge files in this package | **2** (this README and the glossary) |

---

sections.heading: The files
sections.intro:
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| **`00_README.md`** | This file |
| **`07_PLAIN_ENGLISH_GLOSSARY.md`** | Every technical term the notes introduce, defined in plain language, no citations |
| **`09_SOURCE_CATALOG.md`** | All 3 videos — ID, title, URL, upload date, duration, subjects. **Generated mechanically from the notes**, so it stays complete as more videos are added |

A fuller synthesis — cross-cutting principles, a topic-by-topic settings reference, deeper
comparison of flight technique across sources — is deliberately not written yet. With only three
notes from one channel, that kind of synthesis would mostly be restating one note's own words;
per this project's standing practice, whether to add it is a judgement call revisited as more
videos are added, not a gap to paper over now.

---

sections.heading: What the package covers
sections.intro:
- **Menu-by-menu settings walkthroughs for the DJI Air 3S** — flight checklist limits, obstacle
  avoidance modes, return-to-home behavior, camera exposure and color profile, gimbal tuning.
- **Physical setup** — fitting propellers and ND filters, binding the controller to the aircraft,
  choosing an ND filter by a shown stop calculation.
- **Automated flight/camera features** — active track, focus track, waypoints, Quick Shots,
  Master Shots, Hyperlapse, and Panorama modes, each demonstrated in the field.

sections.heading: What the package does not cover
sections.intro:
- **Other drone models.** Every source here is specific to the DJI Air 3S; nothing has been
  generalized to other aircraft.
- **Regulatory/legal flight rules** beyond what the sources themselves mention in passing (e.g. a
  400 ft altitude reference). This is not a substitute for reading your own jurisdiction's
  drone regulations.
- **A single channel's point of view, presented as if it were the only one.** All three sources
  are from the same creator; no other channel's technique has been cross-checked against it yet.

sections.heading: 07 — Plain English Glossary
sections.intro:
Every technical term introduced across this knowledge package, defined the way the source
material defines it. Terms are alphabetical, and no citations appear here — see the individual
notes in `notes/` for the `[mm:ss]` anchor each term traces back to.

---

subsections.body:
**AE lock (auto-exposure lock)** — a controller-button assignment that freezes the camera's
automatic exposure reading at whatever it was when the button was pressed, so exposure doesn't
drift as the drone points at brighter or darker parts of a scene during a shot.
subsections.heading: A

subsections.body:
**Bypass (obstacle avoidance mode)** — an obstacle-avoidance setting where the aircraft routes
around a detected obstacle and continues toward its original destination, rather than stopping.
A more aggressive variant, sometimes labeled "nifty," bypasses obstacles with faster, more dynamic
movement and carries its own in-app risk warning.
subsections.heading: B

subsections.body:
**Cruise control** — a controller-button assignment that, once pressed, sustains whatever stick
inputs (direction, altitude change) were active at that moment, so the aircraft continues that
same motion hands-off until cancelled.
subsections.heading: C

subsections.body:
**D-Log M** — a flat, low-contrast camera color profile intended to preserve detail for color
grading in video-editing software, in contrast to the default "normal" profile that looks correct
straight out of the camera.
subsections.heading: D

subsections.body:
**Gain and Expo tuning** — the settings page (sometimes confused for a differently-named menu)
that controls gimbal movement speed, brake sensitivity, and stick-response curves, separately
configurable for each flight mode (cine, normal, sport).
subsections.heading: G

subsections.body:
**Master Shots** — an automated shot mode that generates a short sequence of varied camera
movements around one selected subject, built from parameters the pilot sets (movement width,
distance from subject, start position).
subsections.heading: M

subsections.body:
**Optimal (return-to-home routing)** — a return-to-home mode where the aircraft calculates and
flies the most efficient path back to the pilot, rather than retracing its outbound flight path
or using a fixed preset route.
subsections.heading: O

subsections.body:
**Quick Shots** — a set of six pre-programmed automated camera movements available from a single
subject selection: Dronie (pulls up and away), Rocket (climbs straight up), Circle (orbits at a
fixed radius), Helix (spirals outward while ascending), Boomerang (an elliptical out-and-back
path), and Asteroid (ascends while capturing a photo series that gets stitched into a tiny-planet
sphere).
subsections.heading: Q

sections.body:
**This video works through the Air 3S's menus tip-by-tip (44 in total) rather than around a
single flight, prioritizing settings the presenter judges worth changing from default over an
exhaustive menu tour.** `[00:00]` "I have 44 tips and settings for the DJI [Air 3S]." Several
tips are explicitly flagged as new to this model rather than carried over: `[00:00]` face
tracking/face focus "is brand new, I've never seen this before on a DJI drone."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
| Tip | Feature | Recommendation / detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Face tracking / face focus | On by default; keeps the presenter's face in focus automatically `[00:00]` |
| 2 | Flight checklist / auto-RTH altitude | "The only thing that I would recommend changing would be the auto return to home altitude" `[01:01]` |
| 3–4 | Focus track (finger box-draw) / touch-screen gimbal control | Press-hold-drag on screen to look up/down/left/right `[01:01]`–`[02:01]` |
| 5 | Waypoints | Set via a dedicated waypoints icon and map tap `[02:01]` |
| 6–7 | Active track button / focus-track sub-modes | Spotlight (follow), point-of-interest (orbit), active track 360, auto `[03:02]`–`[04:03]` |
| 8 | Auto exposure lock | Tap subject, press-hold to lock exposure at that reading `[04:03]` |
| 9 | Map interface | Tap to enlarge/minimize; orientation and zoom controls `[05:04]` |
| 10 | Attitude indicator | Bottom-right map icon shows the aircraft's bank angle in real time `[05:04]` |
sections.heading: Flight menu (00:00–10:09)

sections.body:
The obstacle-avoidance action is presented as a graded choice, not a single on/off: `[11:09]`
"obstacle avoidance action is off... if I flew towards a tree it wouldn't notice the tree and it
would hit the tree. The other option I have is brake... [or] bypass, which is my favorite one...
it does a really good job of avoiding obstacles" — with a more aggressive "nifty" bypass variant
flagged as riskier: "it does give you a warning cuz it's a little bit more risky." Return-to-home
altitude is given a specific recommended range rather than a single number: `[12:11]` "I would
recommend anywhere from 80 m to 100 m." One safety toggle is called out with an explicit
consequence if disabled: `[15:13]` "Vision positioning and obstacle sensing... normally checks
out what's underneath the drone so that it stops at a certain point... if you disable that, the
drone can literally crash down to the ground and bounce off the ground. So I wouldn't recommend
it in most scenarios."
sections.heading: Safety menu (10:09–16:14)

sections.body:
Focus-track radius/height parameters for active track 360 are adjustable per subject type:
`[16:14]` "we can change the inner radius, we can change the outer radius, so we can change that
all the way up to 20 m... I think the lowest is 4 m." Gimbal/Expo tuning is named as the setting
formerly confused for something else: `[17:15]` "this is actually where you go in to change a lot
of the gimbal settings... cine, normal, [and] sport" each with distinct max speed and brake
sensitivity, plus a smoothness parameter that trades responsiveness for a cinematic trail effect:
`[18:16]` "if I put that right up... it's going to slowly trail to make it look a little bit more
cinematic. Now if I pull that right down, you'll see it's more jarring, it's more jumpy." FPV mode
is described as a visual style choice, not a different flight envelope: `[19:17]` "it gives you
more of that FPV effect while still having the control of a drone that's just going to hover and
fly as safely as possible." On the camera side, the presenter recommends enabling the
overexposure warning and grid lines/crosshair as standing defaults: `[23:22]` "it will just let
you know if things are overexposed"; `[23:22]` grid lines plus a center crosshair are "the one[s]
that I prefer having... enabled."
sections.heading: Control and camera menus (16:14–24:23)

sections.body:
Cruise control is defined precisely: `[20:18]` "any input you put into the drone straight when
you press cruise control... it's just going to continue doing those two stick inputs that I put
in." The presenter frames it as worth assigning to a programmable button given how useful it is:
`[20:18]` calling it "really cool, which is a whole feature on its own."
sections.heading: Cruise control and button customization (20:18–21:19)

sections.body:
`[25:24]` frequency band: "by default it's on dual band... you can then swap into 5.8 GHz... [or]
2.4 GHz to see what the interference is like in the area," recommended only as a diagnostic step
when range is poor, not a default change. `[27:26]` firmware: "always do a test flight after
doing these updates." `[27:26]` full reset before selling: "make sure that you unlink your
account from the drone and then... reset all the settings and... clear all the data." `[29:29]`
app cache: aircraft flight records and local logs "can start to fill up" and should be cleared
periodically.
sections.heading: Transmission, about, and housekeeping menus (25:24–29:29)

sections.body:
- **Obstacle avoidance set to "off" will not stop the aircraft**: `[11:09]` explicitly, "it
  wouldn't notice the tree and it would hit the tree."
- **Disabling vision positioning removes the ground-proximity stop**: `[15:13]` "the drone can
  literally crash down to the ground and bounce off the ground," recommended only for
  experienced pilots in open areas at low altitude.
- **A max-altitude increase attempt is gated by a legal warning**: `[11:09]` "if you do try to
  increase it, it comes up with a warning letting you know that it is a breach of laws and
  regulations."
- **Battery percentage readout carries three named thresholds, not just a percentage**:
  `[09:07]` at 34% the display showed "6 minutes [to] return to home... 8 minutes [to] force a
  landing... 10 minutes 55 [to] completely depleted... that's the danger zone you don't want to
  get anywhere near."
- **A firmware update should be followed by a test flight before normal use**: `[27:26]` "always
  do a test flight after doing these updates."
sections.heading: Warnings and pilot signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Bypass / bypass-nifty (obstacle avoidance)** — bypass routes around a detected obstacle
  rather than stopping; the "nifty" variant is a more aggressive bypass behavior flagged with its
  own in-app warning `[11:09]`.
- **Cruise control** — holds whatever stick inputs were active at the moment the assigned button
  is pressed, sustaining that motion hands-off `[20:18]`.
- **Gain and Expo tuning** — the presenter's clarification that this menu (previously named
  differently) is the gimbal-speed and control-response tuning page, not a separate feature
  `[17:15]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body: - None stated as such in this source — it is a direct settings enumeration throughout.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
Every recommendation here is explicitly the presenter's own preference among available options,
not a manufacturer-mandated setting, and the video repeatedly marks that distinction:

- **Obstacle-avoidance mode is stated as personal preference among three named options**:
  `[11:09]` "bypass, which is my favorite one... this one is the one I use all the time purely
  because it gives a dynamic kind of viewing perspective."
- **RTH altitude is given as a recommended range, not a single required value**: `[12:11]`
  "anywhere from 80 m to 100 m."
- **The low-altitude/vision-positioning override is scoped explicitly to experienced pilots in
  controlled conditions**: `[15:13]` "if you need to fly really low and you are an experienced
  pilot and there's no one around."
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
Against `Ogxc6CLBgpc`: both videos recommend "bypass" for obstacle avoidance and "optimal" for
RTH routing, and both flag return-to-home altitude as the one flight-checklist value worth
customizing — this video gives a specific range (80–100 m) where `Ogxc6CLBgpc` only shows the
presenter's own value (100 m) without stating a recommended range, so the two converge rather
than conflict. Neither video states a minimum satellite count before takeoff (`Ogxc6CLBgpc` waits
for "enough," this video doesn't address satellite count directly) — worth resolving if a future
source in this library gives a specific number.

videos.title: DJI Air 3S - 44 Tips & Settings: The Complete Beginners Guide

sections.body:
**This is a first-flight walkthrough for the Air 3S specifically, framed around what changed
from the older Air 3 (sensor, obstacle-avoidance hardware, internal storage) before any flying
starts, then a full pre-flight checklist before takeoff.** `[00:00]` "In today's video we're
going to be doing the beginner guide to the [Air 3S], all the new features, all the upgrades,
and how to get started with your first flight." The hardware framing is explicit about what
carries over versus what's new: `[01:00]` "the battery in itself is exactly the same as the Air
3... that's not very common for them to actually keep the same battery from model to model.
Same for the propellers."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
- **Sensor and obstacle avoidance**: `[00:00]` "This is a 50 megapixel [sensor] instead of 48
  megapixel, f1.8 although the [Air 3] was f1.7... the filters, if you're wondering, do not fit
  if you have Air 3 filters, these are brand new filters." The front obstacle-avoidance bar "now
  uses [LiDAR]... the functionality is exactly the same except the technology is a little bit
  different, so this is supposed to be getting better obstacle information compared to what we
  had before, which was using just cameras."
- **Storage**: `[01:00]` "42 gigs of internal storage compared to — I actually don't remember
  what it was in the Air 3, but I think it was a lot less."
- **Low light and return to home**: `[01:00]` "one of the big advantages of the [LiDAR] is that
  as far as low light conditions, this will be a lot better... also as far as return to home, we
  have the advanced return to home, which is a bit smarter than it was before, where it's going
  to be able to find the most optimal way of getting back to the user."
- **Flight time trade-off, stated as a measured comparison rather than a spec-sheet number**:
  `[01:00]`–`[02:02]` "from our testing we had a minute and 40 seconds less than the Air 3 in the
  same exact environment. Now, is that noticeable? I don't know."
sections.heading: What changed from the Air 3 (00:00–02:02)

sections.body:
| Check | What to look for | Source guidance |
|---|---|---|
| Flight mode switch | N / S / C on the controller | `[02:02]` "N for normal, S would be for sport mode, and then C would be for cinematic" |
| RTH altitude | Set above the tallest obstacle nearby | `[03:03]` set to clear "the tallest tree or the tallest building that you have around"; presenter uses 180 ft |
| Max altitude | 400 ft default legal ceiling, raise only if terrain requires it | `[03:03]` "if you live in a flat area and you don't want to exceed 400 ft you probably want to sit that at 400, 450 ft just to stay within limits" |
| Obstacle avoidance mode | Bypass recommended | `[04:06]` "right now we have it on bypass, which is great, I'm going to keep it as it is" |
| RTH routing | Optimal | `[04:06]` "as far as the RTH we have it set to optimal... it's a good way for the drone to come back and use the most optimal route" |
| Camera profile | Normal vs. D-Log M, manual white balance | `[04:06]`–`[05:08]` "I recommend getting off of the automatic white balance, we set ours to 5600 so all of our cameras match" |
| Weather | Visual wind check (or an app) | `[05:08]` "just look outside, see if the wind feels like it's really moving you around, in which case you don't want to fly" |
| Airspace | Airspace-authorization app | `[05:08]` "you can download an app called [B4UFLY/AirControl]... to see if you need approval" |
| Satellites | Wait for a strong lock before takeoff | `[06:09]` presenter notes "28 satellites" before takeoff, described as "enough satellites to take off" |
sections.heading: Pre-flight checklist (02:02–06:09)

sections.body:
The manual technique is given as a specific dual-stick input, not just "circle the subject":
`[10:14]` "we're going to be using the yaw on the left side here... using the right stick going
to the right and the left stick going to the left at the same time... you will need to use the
right stick to go forward a little bit as well at the same time in order to not get too far away
from your subject." The automated equivalent is presented as easier but less reliable at
recognizing the subject: `[11:16]` "you would have to go on the screen, highlight your subject,
hope that it picks it up... now go in the direction where we want to go to record." Both produce
comparable results in the presenter's own assessment: `[12:16]` "we'll see which one looks best,
my shot or the automated shot."
sections.heading: Manual vs. automated point-of-interest orbit (09:14–12:16)

sections.body:
Active track is demonstrated on a car and then a person, with a caution about staying within
sight and airspace awareness: `[13:17]` "we're still within visual line of sight... [there's]
another airplane nearby, I am nowhere near where they would be, but you would want to be looking
around to see if anybody is coming in your airspace." Return to home is shown triggered manually
near critical battery: `[16:21]` "our battery is actually getting pretty low, we have 4 minutes
left, we just got a warning... I'm going to push the home button here and hold it... it's going
to return to home... it's telling us exactly where it's going to go in 3D." The video ends with
an explicit caution against repeating its own margin: `[17:22]` "we are at critical battery
voltage... we pushed it a little too long, I don't recommend going to that level if you can
avoid it."
sections.heading: Active track and return to home (13:17–17:22)

sections.body:
- **Low battery return-to-home trigger**: `[16:21]` a 4-minutes-remaining warning preceded the
  manual RTH trigger in this flight.
- **Critical battery voltage as a hard stop**: `[17:22]` explicitly flagged as pushed too far —
  "I don't recommend going to that level if you can avoid it."
- **Nearby manned aircraft as an active watch item, not just a one-time check**: `[13:17]` "man,
  aircraft nearby... you would want to be looking around to see if anybody is coming in your
  airspace."
- **Flying over water calls for closer visual monitoring during RTH/landing**: `[16:21]` "you
  want to make sure that you keep an eye on the drone... especially when you're over [half]
  water like we are right here."
- **Satellite count as a pre-takeoff gate**: `[06:09]` presenter waits for a high satellite count
  before takeoff, "we have enough satellites to take off."
sections.heading: Warnings and pilot signals addressed

sections.body:
- **Bypass (obstacle avoidance mode)** — the drone routes around a detected obstacle and
  continues on its path, as opposed to stopping; the presenter's preferred setting `[04:06]`.
- **Optimal (RTH routing)** — an advanced return-to-home mode that calculates "the most optimal
  route" back to the pilot rather than a fixed path `[04:06]`.
- **D-Log M** — a flat, low-contrast color profile intended for color grading in post-production,
  contrasted here with the default "normal" profile `[04:06]`.

- None stated as such in this source — it is direct settings/procedure instruction throughout,
  not illustrative comparison.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
This is a hands-on demo narrated by the presenter's own testing and preference, not a
manufacturer spec sheet, and it marks several claims as exactly that:

- **The flight-time deficit versus the Air 3 is stated as the presenter's own test result, then
  explicitly left unresolved as a buying consideration**: `[01:00]`–`[02:02]` "from our testing we
  had a minute and 40 seconds less... is that noticeable? I don't know... I'm going to let you
  decide if this is something that you can hold against this new drone."
- **The manual-vs-automated orbit comparison is left as an open question rather than a stated
  winner**: `[12:16]` "we'll see which one looks best."
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
No other drone-flight note exists yet to compare against — this is the library's first note. Two
things worth checking once `Dy3xVuIED9c` and `zpJUr_GKVXU` are written: whether their recommended
return-to-home altitude and obstacle-avoidance defaults match this video's "bypass" and "optimal"
recommendations, and whether their stated satellite-count thresholds before takeoff agree with
the "enough to take off" framing used here rather than a specific minimum number.

sections.body:
**This is a physical setup and full-menu walkthrough filmed in the field, going from unboxing
(props, filters, charging) through controller binding to every automated shot mode the Air 3S
offers, before landing on the presenter's own recommended button and exposure setup.** `[00:00]`
"I'm going to go through absolutely everything in this video, from fixing the props, charging the
battery, going through how to fit the ND filters, which ND filter to use, all the features on
the [RC] controller, how to set it up, how to program the buttons, and how to use tracking, quick
shots, master shots, cruise control, and the best settings to use for video and photography — and
we're going to do it all out in the field."
sections.heading: Central claim

sections.body:
Props are keyed to prevent misassembly: `[02:02]` "there's A and B props and it's clearly marked
on the packet here, and it shows you which prop arm to connect them to, and they go diagonally."
Controller-to-aircraft binding requires an explicit hold sequence: `[05:06]` "you hold your
finger down on that and then it'll ask you to hold down the button for 4 seconds on the drone, it
would make a high-pitched bleep a couple of times and they will connect together."

ND filter choice is derived from a specific stop calculation rather than a rule of thumb: `[09:11]`
"I've set the ISO at 100 and we know it needs to be at f2.8 because that's what the fixed focal
length is... [at 400th shutter] to work out which filter you use you would move it one stop up
or down." Following the 180-degree shutter rule at 25 fps: `[10:13]` "180 rule says I want my
shutter to be [1/50th]... I've got to come down three stops... an nd2 is one stop, nd4, nd8 — so
I need to put an nd8 on to get the shutter where I want it to be... I will leave the ISO in auto
and let that just adjust according to the light, but that will give me a better sense of motion
blur in the movements."
sections.heading: Physical setup: props, binding, ND filters (01:01–09:11)

sections.body:
The presenter states his own working assignment rather than a manufacturer default: `[07:09]`
"the C1 button, I've set as cruise control." For C2: `[08:10]` "I've got auto exposure lock on or
off, because I find that super helpful... that's really handy when you're flying — you've got a
good exposure, you don't want it to fluctuate — you can just click that C2 button and it will
hold that exposure throughout any movements you're doing."
sections.heading: Button customization: C1/C2 (07:09–08:10)

sections.body:
Satellite count before this flight was lower than the presenter's usual target, stated as
acceptable rather than a hard minimum: `[10:13]` "checking my satellites, it got to about 11
satellites... it usually likes about 16, of course you only need four to really position where
you are, but one might drop off — that's why it will give you the benefit of having [a] desire
[for] more satellite connections." Active-track geometry is set to specific, stated values before
flying: `[11:13]` "I've changed the inner radius to 5 m, outer radius to 10 m, and the inner
height to 5 m... [and] outer height 10 m, so I know exactly where it's going to be."
sections.heading: Pre-flight and exposure setup in the field (10:13–13:14)

sections.body:
| Mode | What it does | Source detail |
|---|---|---|
| Master Shots | Auto-generates a series of movements from one selected subject | `[24:00]` "you can set all different parameters here... width of the movement, the length away from you, start point location... it just gives you a handful of creative shots to select from" |
| Quick Shots — Dronie | Pulls up and away from the subject | `[25:02]`–`[26:05]` "this will just pull up and away and just give a nice shot of us" |
| Quick Shots — Rocket | Climbs straight up from a low start | `[26:05]` "starting quite low here, 5 m off the ground, so that we get a nice sense of this pulling away" |
| Quick Shots — Circle | Orbits the subject at a fixed radius | `[26:05]` "nicely cruising around us" |
| Quick Shots — Helix | Spirals outward while ascending, radius adjustable | `[26:05]`–`[27:05]` "maximum radius that I want it to do, 10, 20, 30 m, up to 120 m... this will do a nice big spiral out — beautiful motion, one of my favorites" |
| Quick Shots — Boomerang | Elliptical out-and-back path | `[27:05]` "a lovely little elliptical motion which looks fantastic" |
| Quick Shots — Asteroid | Ascends while taking a photo series, stitched into a tiny-planet sphere | `[28:06]` "we'll take a series of images at the top, stitch all together" |
| Hyperlapse | Free-fly, circle, course, or waypoint-driven timelapse | `[28:06]`–`[29:07]` "you can free-fly it and it will just take lots of series of images [and] stitch them together... or we can circulate something, we can create a course, or do it via waypoints" |
| Free Panorama | Presenter sets a start and end framing point, then the aircraft captures and stitches the sphere | `[29:07]`–`[30:08]` "you use the C1 button as your first frame, and then you can create your last frame there... click start and it will take that series of photos" |
sections.heading: Automated shot modes (24:00–30:08)

sections.body:
The waypoint workflow ties recording start/stop to specific waypoints and can force the gimbal to
hold on a fixed subject throughout: `[20:50]`–`[21:53]` "we're going to go to our waypoint one and
say this is where we're going to start recording, and then we're going to go to waypoint two and
this is where it's going to stop recording... if we get to our point of interest [and set]
altitude... to zero, that's going to make it look at me [as a] point of interest... the gimbal
should always be looking at me."
sections.heading: Waypoint flight with point-of-interest lock (20:50–22:56)

sections.body:
- **Satellite count below the presenter's usual target is treated as acceptable, not a stop
  condition, provided it's above the stated functional minimum**: `[10:13]` "you only need four
  to really position where you are, but one might drop off — that's why it will give you the
  benefit of having more satellite connections" as a margin, not a hard rule.
- **A firmware update prompt is treated as expected and to be completed before flying**: `[06:06]`
  "when you first buy them you will get an immediate update required... always do a test flight
  after doing these updates."
- **Auto-exposure lock is framed as a way to prevent unwanted exposure hunting mid-shot**:
  `[08:10]` "you don't want it to fluctuate... it's not continually trying to adjust whether it's
  looking at the sky or the ground."
sections.heading: Warnings and pilot signals addressed

sections.body:
- **AE lock (C2 shortcut)** — a programmable button assignment that freezes auto-exposure at its
  current reading for the duration of a shot `[08:10]`.
- **Quick Shots** — a named set of six pre-programmed automated camera movements (Dronie, Rocket,
  Circle, Helix, Boomerang, Asteroid), each launched from a single subject selection `[25:02]`.
- **Master Shots** — an auto-generated sequence of varied movements around one selected subject,
  built from presenter-set parameters (width, distance, start point) `[24:00]`.
sections.heading: Glossary terms introduced

sections.body:
- **"A little mini world"** `[28:06]` — describing the tiny-planet look of the stitched Asteroid
  shot.
sections.heading: Analogies worth reusing

sections.body:
This is a hands-on, in-the-field demonstration of the presenter's own working setup, and it
marks personal-preference choices as such rather than presenting them as the only correct
configuration:

- **The C1/C2 button assignments are stated as the presenter's own choice, not a required
  configuration**: `[07:09]`–`[08:10]` "I've set [C1] as cruise control... [for C2] I've got auto
  exposure lock... because I find that super helpful."
- **The ND-filter selection is derived from an explicit, shown calculation rather than asserted
  as a fixed rule**: `[09:11]`–`[10:13]` the stop-counting walkthrough is presented as the method,
  with the specific filter (nd8) following from that day's light reading, not as a universal
  choice.
- **The lower-than-usual satellite count is explicitly qualified as still workable**: `[10:13]`
  "of course you only need four... one might drop off," rather than claiming 11 was ideal.
sections.heading: Source-stated confidence

sections.body:
Against `Dy3xVuIED9c`: both videos cover active-track/focus-track radius and height parameters,
and both frame C1/C2 (or equivalent) button customization as a place to assign cruise control —
converging recommendations, not a conflict. Against `Ogxc6CLBgpc`: that video shows a manual
dual-stick point-of-interest orbit technique `Ogxc6CLBgpc`[10:14]; this video achieves a
comparable gimbal-locked point-of-interest shot through waypoints and altitude-zero targeting
instead `[21:53]` — two different paths to the same framing goal, worth noting as alternatives rather
than a disagreement. No source in this library yet gives a single minimum satellite count before
takeoff; this video's "you only need four" is the most specific figure so far and should be
checked against future sources.
